chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: The act stays the same from theatre to theatre
summary: His act was always top; he repeated it in each theatre because only the audience changed, and traveling was second nature.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So what was happening basically with your relationship with Buck at this point. He was married and you were married, too, weren't you at this time?
At this point -- I've forgotten whether I was married before I went to New York -- I married before I went to New York. I think I did, yeah.
So your wife was traveling with you.
And what was happening basically with your act. It was getting better, I take it.
My act was about the same always. Never had to worry about it's being better , it was tops at the time. Didn't worry about it getting better. If it was better I'd have to stop working.
of the things you had in your repertoire -- and I'm sure you didn't do the same thing all the time. You probably varied it.

Yeah, got to do the same thing all the time because we're changing theaters. Don't need to put a new act on in every theater we went. Do the same act in different theaters. Change the public, change the audiences.
Well, were you yourself responding differently -- what were you learning about an audience, what were you learning about -- what was it like traveling on the road?
Well, I'd been traveling for so long, it was just like second nature. Good traveling.
